provider.notes: Registered as speechmatics with aliases speech-matics and speech_matics (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:185-201, :1719), plus speechmatics-stt in the static dispatch table (gateway/src/plugin/dispatch.rs:294). Only the spelling speechmatics reaches the standardized factory (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:461); the aliases take the flat factory, which drops the standardized features (standard.rs:476), so the resolver must normalise the provider id before lookup. default_model is standard because the vendor uses it when no model is sent, and the client sends none for an empty model (gateway/src/core/stt/speechmatics/config.rs:522-524). The client's model gate is a substring match (config.rs:526-531): any id containing 'standard' or 'enhanced' selects an operating point. The short aliases std, enh and high (config.rs:100-101) are model aliases of the standard and enhanced rows, and the placeholder nova-3, which the client reads as unset (config.rs:485, :522), is covered by key_normalisation; the substring rule has no field, so the resolver must apply it before lookup or those sessions fall to the provider default row. Every other id, including melia-1, oak-1 and linden-1, is refused by name at construction (config.rs:536-540). The melia-1 and oak-1 rows are the least stable facts in this file: the vendor planned a realtime release for October 2026, so they carry a re-check date and need a probe with a key. The batch hosts are eu1, us1 and au1 (eu2 and us2 also exist, for Enterprise failover only). Batch jobs are bound to the regional host that created them, melia-1 and oak-1 exist only on the EU1 and US1 hosts (a region constraint on their batch transports), and the client can only dial the EU realtime host (config.rs:652). The batch service stores audio and transcripts for 7 days unless the job is deleted; the realtime socket stores nothing.

languages.note: Speechmatics documents automatic language detection ('auto') for batch transcription only (confirmed by the fact-check). Today's client accepts 'auto' and sends it; how the socket reacts is not established.

latency.notes: Not measured for the gateway's client. Pipecat lists SPEECHMATICS_TTFS_P99 at 0.74 s (end of speech to final transcript, voice-activity stop time 200 ms, model and client settings not stated), but that figure does not describe this transport: the gateway's client always sets max_delay to 2 seconds, never sends ForceEndOfUtterance and leaves the vendor's silence trigger off by default, so its finals are released on the 2-second max_delay timer (gateway/src/core/stt/speechmatics/mod.rs:59, client.rs:418-420, :468-470), and they are not marked speech-final, so the gateway's transcript timers add their own wait before the turn ends. The real figure is expected to be near 2 seconds or more (inferred from the code and the vendor's definition of max_delay; not measured). Record a number here only from the gateway's own probe.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock server. Finals are word groups released on the vendor's max_delay timer, which the client always sets to 2 seconds (mod.rs:59, client.rs:420). They are marked final but not speech-final, so the gateway's transcript timers end the turn, unless the session sets utterance_end_ms, which turns on the vendor's silence trigger (config.rs:753-755, client.rs:468-470). The client sends the deprecated operating_point field, never model, always dials the EU host (config.rs:652), and accepts the language value 'auto', which the vendor documents as batch only. gateway_client.notes: Needs a multipart request with a 'config' part (JSON using model, not operating_point) and a 'data_file' part, bearer authentication, a per-region https base URL (the existing endpoint override accepts only ws and wss), handling of the job states created, done, rejected and deleted, and a best-effort delete of the job afterwards. segment_profile.rationale: The request is POST /v2/jobs/?wait=10&format=json-v2, which blocks until the job finishes or the wait elapses, so each HTTP call gets 12 seconds, slightly longer than the wait. If the job is still running the adapter makes one GET of the transcript with a wait, then fails the segment. The server caps the wait at an unpublished value. The adapter should delete each job after reading it, because the batch service keeps audio for 7 days. All other defaults hold: the vendor names 16-bit 16 kHz mono WAV as the fastest format for very short files and bills to the second.

billing.notes: Batch is a different product type from realtime, with its own rate, priced in credits per hour of audio and billed to the second. Only uploaded speech segments are billed. pricing.rs has no Speechmatics speech-to-text key.

gateway_client.notes: Needs a multipart request with a 'config' part (JSON using model, not operating_point) and a 'data_file' part, bearer authentication, a per-region https base URL (the existing endpoint override accepts only ws and wss), handling of the job states created, done, rejected and deleted, and a best-effort delete of the job afterwards. The blocking wait parameter exists only on the hosted service; a self-hosted batch container needs submit and poll.

segment_profile.rationale: The request is POST /v2/jobs/?wait=10&format=json-v2, which blocks until the job finishes or the wait elapses, so each HTTP call gets 12 seconds, slightly longer than the wait. If the job is still running the adapter makes one GET of the transcript with a wait, then fails the segment. The server caps the wait at an unpublished value. The adapter should delete each job after reading it, because the batch service keeps audio for 7 days. All other defaults hold: the vendor names 16-bit 16 kHz mono WAV as the fastest format for very short files and bills to the second.
